subject.title: Heartbeat: Use ISO 8601 for Current time and separate trigger timestamp

question: Should the shared cron-style current-time prompt contract move to ISO 8601 everywhere, add a heartbeat-only trigger timestamp, or be handled as part of the broader prompt-cache timestamp-placement work?
rationale: The requested change touches a shared model-visible prompt helper and overlaps prompt-cache behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent prompt contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve shared timestamp contract
options.body: Use one explicit contract for heartbeat, cron, reset, status, and compaction prompt timestamps, then implement and test the shared helper and heartbeat trigger plumbing together.

options.title: Limit to heartbeat only
options.body: Keep the shared helper unchanged and add a heartbeat-specific trigger timestamp if maintainers want the smallest visible change for this issue.

options.title: Defer to cache redesign
options.body: Keep this issue open behind the broader prompt-cache timestamp-placement decision if volatile timestamp location matters more than formatting right now.

recommendation.title: Approve shared timestamp contract
recommendation.body: Use one explicit contract for heartbeat, cron, reset, status, and compaction prompt timestamps, then implement and test the shared helper and heartbeat trigger plumbing together.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the shared heartbeat/cron current-time prompt contract and are the clearest history owner for deciding whether that contract should change globally.
